title: Braxton County solidifies status as West Virginia's 2026 boating capital | News | wvnews.com
text:
SUTTON, W.Va. — Nestled in the heart of the Appalachian Mountains, Braxton County has established itself in 2026 as a premier regional hub for boating enthusiasts, offering a diverse array of water-based recreation across two massive federal reservoirs and the state's longest interior river.
Anchored by the expansive waters of Sutton Lake and Burnsville Lake, both managed by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, the county provides over 2,400 acres of navigable lake surface in addition to the winding Elk River Water Trail. According to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and the Braxton County Convention and Visitors Bureau, these facilities are designed to accommodate everything from high-speed motorboats and houseboats to serene kayak expeditions.
